questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Always look ahead and expect possible dangers.
Focus on the controls and speedometer instead of the road.
Not worry about hazards because they are rare on roads.
Look ahead but avoid looking for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always look ahead and expect possible dangers.
questions.explanation: Look well ahead to spot hazards early. This gives you time to react before you reach them.

questions.question: Which clothing item will NOT help reduce crash injuries?

options.text: Heavy shoes
Full-length pants
Shorts
Full-fingered gloves

questions.correctAnswerText: Shorts
questions.explanation: Wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Use durable materials for the best protection.

questions.question: Smoothly downshifting on motorcycles:

options.text: Does nothing useful.
Helps slow the motorcycle using engine power.
Is against the law.
Should not be done around other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps slow the motorcycle using engine power.
questions.explanation: Engine braking through downshifting is useful for slowing down. Use your brake lights to alert other drivers that you are slowing.

questions.question: When stopped behind another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Get as close as possible to the vehicle.
Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
Not use your rearview mirrors to check traffic behind you.
Look for chances to squeeze through stopped traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle ahead, even when stopped. This gives you room to escape if the vehicle backs up or another vehicle approaches quickly from behind.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: You have been drinking alcohol. If you wait one hour per drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
Alcohol effects may still be present.
You will be fine if you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still be present.
questions.explanation: Your body can process about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can still build up. Your ability to judge situations and ride safely can still be impaired.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Assume they have ridden on a motorcycle before.
Not assume they have ridden before and explain what to do.
Not let them ask questions.
Not explain anything since they are just a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume they have ridden before and explain what to do.
questions.explanation: Passengers need to understand how to stay safe. Never assume a passenger knows what to do. Give clear instructions before every ride.

questions.question: Goggles will:

options.text: Protect only your eyes.
Work as well as a face shield.
Provide the same protection as a windshield.
Protect your entire face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect only your eyes.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only, not your whole face. A face shield protects your entire face and is better than goggles. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: The front brake is:

options.text: Safe when used correctly.
Safe even if used incorrectly.
Only for use if the rear brake fails.
Not meant for regular use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safe when used correctly.
questions.explanation: The front brake is safe when used properly. It provides more stopping power than the rear brake, giving at least three-fourths of total stopping power.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should:

options.text: Pick one spot in the lane and always stay there.
Move around the lane to keep other drivers out.
Choose a lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Not worry about where in the lane to ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position based on what is happening on the road and with traffic.

questions.question: If you think your motorcycle will take longer than usual to stop, what should you do?

options.text: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Decrease the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Leave the road.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead. If your motorcycle needs more time to stop, leave more space between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: What type of footwear is best for riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Sturdy boots
Tennis shoes
Shoes with loose laces
Sandals

questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy boots or high-top shoes that support your ankles. Laced boots work best. If your laces are long, tuck them in securely before riding.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce the risk of head or neck injury in a crash?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder
Ride under the speed limit
Wear a helmet
Don't allow passengers on your motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a helmet
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most effective way to reduce head and neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure your motorcycle is equipped and set up for a passenger.
Ride the same way as you would without a passenger.
Have footrests only for yourself, the operator.
Tell the passenger what to do after you start riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your motorcycle is equipped and set up for a passenger.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have the right equipment for a passenger. This includes separate footrests for the passenger, a seat big enough for two people, and possibly adjustments to the headlight, tire pressure, and suspension for the extra weight.

questions.question: What is a simple way to make your motorcycle easier to see?

options.text: Attach a large flag to the frame.
Keep your headlight on.
Wave at other drivers.
Ride on the shoulder whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. Also wear bright colors and reflective clothing, and use your turn signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: What should you do before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle?

options.text: Ride it like your own bike, since all bikes are the same.
Check the controls and gear shift pattern.
Trust the owner that everything works.
Assume you know where all the controls are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the controls and gear shift pattern.
questions.explanation: All motorcycles are different. Check the controls and learn the gear pattern before riding. Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times first.

questions.question: What is true about an approved helmet?

options.text: It lets you see as far to the sides as you need to.
It limits your side vision.
It is usually uncomfortable.
It has no labels or markings.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets you see as far to the sides as you need to.
questions.explanation: An approved helmet allows you to see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding. Approved helmets have labels with the manufacturer's name, instructions, and information about the safety standards they meet.

questions.question: What clothing should you wear when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Clothing that covers your arms and legs completely.
Clothing that covers your arms but leaves your legs exposed.
Clothing that covers your legs but leaves your arms exposed.
Whatever is most comfortable, regardless of safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clothing that covers your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely for proper protection.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: A jacket
Boots
Gloves
A stocking cap

questions.correctAnswerText: A stocking cap
questions.explanation: Protective clothing includes sturdy pants and jackets that cover your arms and legs completely, boots or heavy shoes that cover and support your ankles, and sturdy gloves.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet does NOT have which of the following?

options.text: An impact-resistant outer shell.
An impact-absorbing inner liner.
A chinstrap to hold it in place.
Bright colors painted on the outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright colors painted on the outside.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet must have an impact-resistant outer shell, an impact-absorbing inner liner, a comfort liner, and a chinstrap. Bright colors are not required.

questions.question: What should you wear to help other drivers see you?

options.text: Dark-colored clothes.
Bright-colored clothes.
Lights.
A black jacket.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright-colored clothes.
questions.explanation: Bright colors help other drivers see you. Wear bright clothes during the day and at night to stay visible.

questions.question: How should you check tire pressure?

options.text: Look at the tire.
Use a tire gauge.
Squeeze the tire.
Compare it to another tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a tire gauge.
questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check pressure before riding. A tire can look fine but still be under-inflated, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: Which item is NOT required on a street-legal motorcycle?

options.text: A headlight
Turn signals
Two mirrors
A windshield

questions.correctAnswerText: A windshield
questions.explanation: Street-legal motorcycles must have a headlight, taillight, brake light, front and rear brakes, turn signals, a horn, and two mirrors. A windshield is not required.

questions.question: What is true about motorcycle blind spots?

options.text: Motorcycles do not have blind spots because they are small.
Blind spots are so small they are not a problem.
You should check blind spots regularly.
Motorcycles are too small to have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should check blind spots regularly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your regular scanning routine.

questions.question: What is the purpose of your lane position?

options.text: Hide your plans from other drivers.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see better and be seen better.
Stay close to road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see better and be seen better.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see other vehicles and be seen. It also helps you avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. It discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.
